1 غَزُرَ , aor.
غَزُرَ , inf. n. غَزَارَهٌ (S, Mgh, Msb, K) and غَزْرٌ (Mgh, L, Msb, K) and غُزْرٌ, (L, K,) or غَزْرٌ is a simple subst., (S, L, TA,) It (a thing, S, K, or water, Mgh, Msb) was, or became, much, abundant, or copious. (S, Mgh, Msb, K,) ―
-b2- غَزُرَتْ She (a camel, S, Msb, or a beast, K) bad much milk; abounded in milk, became abundant in milk; (S, Msb, K:) عَنِ الكَلَأ from the (??) (TA;) or عَلَيْهِ [by feeding] upon it; (K;) as also ↓ أَغْزَرَتْ : (IKtt:) and it (a well, and a spring,) abounded in water; and it (an eye) abounded in tears. (K.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
